s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive skin lesions with inflammatory infiltrate and history of local excisions and immunotherapy
salient_findings: New and progressive satellite lesions despite pembrolizumab therapy
Multiple unresectable satellite lesions appeared after initial wide local excision
Local progression occurred in satellite lesions after 5 cycles of pembrolizumab
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 50s
Initial treatment was wide local excision with graft repair for a left posterior auricular scalp lesion
Incidentally resected lymph node was found to be focally involved
No evidence of distant metastatic disease initially
Patient received 4 cycles of ipilimumab
Second wide local excision was performed when new lesions appeared
Pembrolizumab therapy was started due to additional satellite lesions
Local progression occurred in satellite lesions after 5 cycles of pembrolizumab
Histopathology showed intense mixed superficial and deep dermal inflammatory infiltrate
Immunostaining results highlighted normal melanocytes, histiocytes, and neutrophils

shortlist.label: Regression-associated melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of local excisions and immunotherapy with evidence of tumor regression and inflammatory infiltrate

shortlist.label: Nodular melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive nature of the disease with multiple satellite lesions and local progression despite treatment

shortlist.label: Desmoplastic melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of intense mixed inflammatory infiltrate and history of local excisions

shortlist.label: Superficial spreading melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: Initial presentation with a scalp lesion and subsequent development of satellite lesions

shortlist.label: Melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: Primary diagnosis given the patient's history and clinical presentation

raw.rationale: The presence of intense mixed superficial and deep dermal inflammatory infiltrate and the history of local progression despite immunotherapy, along with the clinical regression of lesions and persistent black pigmentation, are consistent with regression-associated melanoma.

rejected.label: Nodular melanoma
rejected.why: Nodular melanoma typically presents as a rapidly growing, pigmented nodule without a radial growth phase, which does not match the patient's history of satellite lesions and regression.

rejected.label: Desmoplastic melanoma
rejected.why: Desmoplastic melanoma is characterized by a dense fibrotic stroma, which is not mentioned in the histopathology findings.

rejected.label: Superficial spreading melanoma
rejected.why: Superficial spreading melanoma typically has a longer radial growth phase and less aggressive behavior than what is described in the patient's history.

rejected.label: Melanoma
rejected.why: Melanoma is a broad category, and while the patient does have melanoma, the specific subtype of regression-associated melanoma better explains the key facts.
